items.stem: An AI vision tool reports a site is 70% complete, but this conflicts with the surveyor's measured progress. What is the responsible action?

options.text: Treat the AI output as an input to verify against site evidence, not as the final truth
options.rationale: Correct: AI outputs should be verified, with humans accountable.

options.text: Automatically overwrite the surveyor's figure with the AI value
options.rationale: Blindly trusting the AI over verified measurement is unsafe.

options.text: Delete the surveyor's report to avoid conflict
Ignore both and guess a number
options.rationale: Guessing discards both the data and the measurement.

items.explanation: Correct: AI outputs should be verified, with humans accountable.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are sensible checks before trusting an AI estimating tool on a real project? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Evaluate its predictions against known past project outcomes
options.rationale: Correct: validating against known outcomes tests fitness for use.

options.text: Confirm the input data is representative and good quality
options.rationale: Correct: poor or unrepresentative data undermines predictions.

options.text: Assume it is correct because it is AI
options.rationale: Assuming correctness without evidence is unsafe.

options.text: Remove human review to save time
options.rationale: Removing human review increases risk on consequential decisions.

items.explanation: Correct: validating against known outcomes tests fitness for use.

items.stem: Why must a named human remain accountable for a safety-critical decision supported by AI?

options.text: Because responsibility for consequences cannot be delegated to a tool, and AI can be wrong
options.rationale: Correct: accountability stays with people; AI can err.

options.text: Because AI tools legally cannot produce any output
options.rationale: AI tools do produce output; the point is accountability.

options.text: Because humans are always faster than software
options.rationale: Speed is not the reason; accountability is.

options.text: Because the tool will refuse to run otherwise
options.rationale: This is not why human accountability is required.

items.explanation: Correct: accountability stays with people; AI can err.
